# Divider

A rule marking a change of topic within a page, or a separation between groups in a toolbar.

**Not implemented yet.** This page is the *approved intent* — the props API signed off at gate 1 of the build order, before any React exists. Do not import it; there is nothing to import.

| | |
|---|---|
| Registry name | `divider` |
| Family | content |
| Tier | free |
| Status (css / react / figma) | future / future / future |
| Depends on | — |

## Behavior

An `<hr>` when horizontal, a `role="separator"` element when vertical, or an `aria-hidden` rule when `decorative`. No primitive: a non-focusable separator has no interaction to own.

- **Most lines in a UI are not Dividers** — The rule between table rows is the table's, the rule between menu groups is `MenuSeparator`, the rule between a stack of Disclosures belongs to the stack, and the outline of a Card is the card's. Each of those is a border owned by the component that knows where it goes. A Divider is for the one case none of them cover: a change of topic in running content, or a group boundary in a row of controls. If you are placing a Divider between every item of a list, the list should own the border.
- **Semantic by default, `decorative` to opt out** — An `<hr>` is a thematic break, announced as a separator, and it tells a screen-reader user what a sighted reader sees: the topic changed here. When the line is only visual — the gap would have done, but the design wants a line — `decorative` hides it so a reader does not hear "separator" between two things that are not separate. Defaulting the other way would make every semantic break silent unless the caller remembered.
- **Vertical is a `role="separator"`, not an `<hr>`** — An `<hr>` is horizontal by definition, and styling one vertical leaves it announcing the wrong orientation. A vertical divider between toolbar groups is a `div` with `role="separator"` and `aria-orientation="vertical"`, which is what the ARIA toolbar pattern expects.
- **No label in the middle** — "— or —" between two sign-in options is a sentence, not a rule, and rendering text inside a separator makes a screen reader either skip the text or read the separator as content. Write the word as text between two decorative dividers if the design needs it. A labelled divider is not part of this gate.
- **Web and native** — Web: `<hr>` horizontally; `<div role="separator" aria-orientation="vertical">` vertically; with `decorative`, the same element with `aria-hidden="true"` (and `role="none"` on the `<hr>`). React Native has no separator role: a hairline `View` that is always hidden from assistive tech with `importantForAccessibility="no"` and `accessibilityElementsHidden`, whatever `decorative` says — the topic change is carried by the heading that follows it, which is the only structure native screen readers navigate by. `decorative` therefore has an effect on web only. Rata-drawn (decision N5): there is no OS separator control. The native implementation ships in the pro tier (decision N6).

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|
| `orientation?` | `"horizontal" \| "vertical"` | `"horizontal"` | Which way the rule runs. |
| `decorative?` | `boolean` | `false` | Hides the rule from assistive tech when it marks no real change of topic. |
| `className?` | `string` | — | Extra classes, for placement. |

### `orientation`

```ts
orientation?: "horizontal" | "vertical" = "horizontal"
```

Which way the rule runs.

**Use when**

- `vertical` between groups of controls in a horizontal row, such as a toolbar.

**Don't use for**

- `vertical` between two columns of a page layout. That is the layout's border, not a separator.

**Accessibility** `horizontal` renders an `<hr>`; `vertical` renders `role="separator"` with `aria-orientation="vertical"`.

### `decorative`

```ts
decorative?: boolean = false
```

Hides the rule from assistive tech when it marks no real change of topic.

**Use when**

- A line the design wants where the content does not change subject — around an "or" between two sign-in options.

**Don't use for**

- Every divider, by habit. A real topic break should be heard as one.

**Accessibility** Adds `aria-hidden="true"`. Web only: on React Native the rule is always hidden.

### `className`

```ts
className?: string
```

Extra classes, for placement.

**Use when**

- The space the page wants either side, which this component deliberately does not own.

**Don't use for**

- A thicker or coloured rule. A heavier boundary is `theme.border.strong` on the component that owns it, not a restyled divider.

## Use cases

### A change of topic in running content

Two parts of a page about different things, where a heading alone would be too quiet.

```tsx
<Text>Your plan renews on 1 March.</Text>
<Divider />
<Heading level={2}>Danger zone</Heading>
```

Semantic, so it is announced as a separator. The space either side comes from the parent's stack gap, not from the divider.

### Groups in a toolbar

A row of controls in two or more groups.

```tsx
<div role="toolbar" aria-label="Formatting">
  <Button variant="tertiary">Bold</Button>
  <Button variant="tertiary">Italic</Button>
  <Divider orientation="vertical" />
  <Button variant="tertiary">Link</Button>
</div>
```

Vertical renders `role="separator"` with `aria-orientation`, which is what the toolbar pattern expects between groups.

### Reaching for the wrong component

A rule between every row of a list.

```tsx
{rows.map((row) => (
  <>
    <Row row={row} />
    <Divider />
  </>
))}
```

Don't. A screen reader hears "separator" between every row, and the list cannot drop the last one cleanly. The list owns its row borders — a Table, or the list's own CSS with `theme.border.default`.

## Token recipe

### base

One hairline in the divider colour `theme.border.default` documents. No margin: the stack it sits in owns the space either side.

| Property | Token |
|---|---|
| border-block-start | `border.default solid theme.border.default` |
| margin | `space.0 — the parent's gap places it, as with Heading` |
| inline-size | `the full width of its container` |

### vertical

The same hairline on the other axis, stretching to the height of the row it divides.

| Property | Token |
|---|---|
| border-inline-start | `border.default solid theme.border.default` |
| block-size | `stretched to the row by the parent's alignment` |
| margin | `space.0` |
